Definition: Jakim, the name of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Jakim is the name of two Israelites, a Benjamite of the line of Shimhi and the head of the twelfth priestly course. One stands in the genealogy of Benjamin, the other in the order of the temple service.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God orders both the tribe and the temple, and the same name can serve in the family and at the altar.
RelatedPeople: Jakim, Son of Shimhi; Jakim, Course Head
